thread.title: Reviews Now Visible for Project Final Drafts
thread.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>Everyone should be able to see their reviews for their final drafts by logging into the "Author" console of the <link href="https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/DLFP2025">conference site</link>. These final reviews should help with polishing your project reports that are due <bold>this Sunday on Gradescope</bold>. </paragraph><paragraph/></document>
thread.document: Everyone should be able to see their reviews for their final drafts by logging into the "Author" console of the conference site. These final reviews should help with polishing your project reports that are due this Sunday on Gradescope.

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>Students should add an appendix to their report that includes two sections:</paragraph><paragraph>1) How their final report has incorporated feedback and insights from the poster session.</paragraph><paragraph>2) A response to the reviewers that shows how the final report has addressed comments and feedback. </paragraph></document>
comments.document:
Students should add an appendix to their report that includes two sections:

1) How their final report has incorporated feedback and insights from the poster session.

2) A response to the reviewers that shows how the final report has addressed comments and feedback.

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>For point 2), do we have to show how the final report addressed comments and feedback from our initial reviews as well, or just the final reviews?</paragraph></document>
comments.document: For point 2), do we have to show how the final report addressed comments and feedback from our initial reviews as well, or just the final reviews?

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>Just the final reviews is fine. If you want, you can be brief and describe the updates you did for the initial reviews. This is particularly important if you found yourself in a situation where you got contradictory advice: the initial reviewers said to change X and then the final reviewers complained about the change. </paragraph><paragraph>The key objective here is for you to document how the review process influenced the final product. Some of this is for your own protection: if the reviewers gave you very bad advice, we need to know that so we don't hold you completely accountable for those mistakes. (In reality and in the grading here, you are responsible for the final quality, coherency, and integrity of your work. You have to stand up for it and do what's right --- the reviewers' mistakes do not remove your responsibility.)</paragraph><paragraph>In many cases, the narrative can be more circuitous: the reviewers noticed X, but when we thought about it, we realized that they were wrong and the actual problem was Y which they hadn't noticed, and so we fixed Y. This is the reality of reviews. They often help your thinking, even when they are wrong. </paragraph></document>
comments.document:
Just the final reviews is fine. If you want, you can be brief and describe the updates you did for the initial reviews. This is particularly important if you found yourself in a situation where you got contradictory advice: the initial reviewers said to change X and then the final reviewers complained about the change. 

The key objective here is for you to document how the review process influenced the final product. Some of this is for your own protection: if the reviewers gave you very bad advice, we need to know that so we don't hold you completely accountable for those mistakes. (In reality and in the grading here, you are responsible for the final quality, coherency, and integrity of your work. You have to stand up for it and do what's right --- the reviewers' mistakes do not remove your responsibility.)

In many cases, the narrative can be more circuitous: the reviewers noticed X, but when we thought about it, we realized that they were wrong and the actual problem was Y which they hadn't noticed, and so we fixed Y. This is the reality of reviews. They often help your thinking, even when they are wrong.
